doc.title: Tyner McCoy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Steinway, Blue Note, awards and wrap-up
title: The Coltrane and Hartman album
summary: They discuss the session, who suggested it, and Tyner's accompaniment of singers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well that album, John Coltrane, Johnny Hartman, I mean I don’t want to get to something that’s on the record, but I think I have had more success with women if I played that record because I mean Johnny Hartman, John Coltrane I mean if you were interested in any kind of romance, you can’t lose. If something doesn’t happen it’s because you messed up. The music was there (both laugh).
Yeah, that’s a great album. I really enjoyed it.
You enjoyed the session, you remember that?
Yeah, I enjoyed the session.
And you know, Johnny Hartman, the voice he had, but he never really broke into the big time, do you have any understanding-
Just like Austin Cromer was another one, and Sonny Rollins loved him and my sister also.
Yeah, her sister was a great singer.

And Loraine used to play Austin the one he did with Dizzy in 1955, but both of them, Johnny Hartman was, you're right. You have to not feel anything if you listen to that and you can’t . . . really I play it all the time.
I know you remember that session but do you remember how it came about, who’s idea was it to marry those two?
I think it was John’s idea.
John loved singers.
Yeah, right.
Like your sister.
That’s why he probably got more from him playing piano than my sister singing.
Yeah, her sister was a great singer.
That’s why he played so beautifully, he was singing when he played the horn.
Yeah John had a beautiful tone.
And that session just flows, it seems to flow. Was that the way it actually went in the studio?
Yeah, actually, yeah.
Played some beautiful stuff . . . oh gosh, you (McCoy) played some beautiful stuff.
If anybody doesn’t know McCoy Tyner, they need to go hear that record. They can hear anything they want with the other quartet but-
My sister loved him so much because the way he played behind vocalists.
Yeah, I did the best I could.
